S1 BLOCKING — Same-slot re-checkout still silently destroys live campaign state.
Invariant/authority: ADR 0012 custody lifecycle requires same-slot re-checkout to be idempotent and protects the active campaign writer from silent loss; ADR 0011 section 4 explicitly makes hp_current and conditions_json authoritative live fields rather than CharacterSheet fields. Owning item #4 requires restoring this no-loss invariant.
Location: packages/core/src/character/characterCustody.ts:202-227 (comparison followed by unconditional attach); downstream packages/core/src/character/creation.ts:470,477.
Concrete scenario: check out a 12-max-HP character, take damage to 3 HP and acquire a condition without changing the build sheet, then call checkoutCharacterIntoCampaign again for the held campaign/slot. The stripped sheet still equals registry head, so the guard passes; importFinalizedCharacter resets hp_current to 12 and conditions_json to []. Source-bound probe returned ok:true and reproduced exactly that reset. The new level-change test never varies the live-row dimension.
Boundary/owner: public core checkout API (root export); CLI normally allocates a free slot, which reduces current CLI reachability but does not remove the accepted API requirement.
Sibling analysis: changed-sheet checkout now refuses correctly; unchanged-sheet and post-sync-back checkout can still lose live-only state. acquireCustodyOnResume already avoids re-attachment precisely to preserve HP/conditions (characterCustody.ts:590-593). catchUpCharacterToHead intentionally replaces a stale copy after an explicit choice and is a different authorized transition.
Closure: make held-same-slot checkout truly preserve authoritative live state, or refuse before any write when it cannot; update the checkout inventory claim to match. Permanent evidence should be a generalized idempotence/no-loss regression covering live-only HP/conditions as well as sheet progress, using the real projection boundary; this inexpensive state test is proportionate to silent state loss.
Repair material: YES (durable lifecycle behavior).

S2 BLOCKING — Failed-attach custody acquisition survives in the catch-up sibling.
Invariant/authority: ADR 0012 attach-before-custody/single-writer lifecycle and owning item #3 require custody only after a successful attachment that establishes the campaign writer; the newly repaired checkout branch itself implements that requirement.
Location: packages/core/src/character/characterCustody.ts:704-725, especially unconditional setCustody at 717 after attach.
Concrete scenario: a registry-linked campaign sheet and registry head share a non-dnd5e system/pack (the same matching unsupported-system state used by the new checkout regression); call public catchUpCharacterToHead. attachCharacterSheetToCampaign saves the sheet, importFinalizedCharacter returns ok:false because the live-row import is unsupported, yet catch-up records custody and returns a result. The source-bound probe reproduced attach.ok:false with a custody row. Its CLI consumer at packages/cli/src/playCharacter.ts:563-590 reports the catch-up and returns success without checking result.attach.ok.
Boundary/owner: core custody/attach result contract and resume consumer. Normal released CLI setup does not construct these unsupported registry sheets; the public API state is expressly admitted by the owning triage and test.
Sibling analysis: checkout now checks attach.ok; catch-up is the other direct attach-and-setCustody path and retains the same defective assumption. Ordinary resume deliberately takes custody without re-importing an already valid attachment; sync-back/release do not perform an attach. Fork routes through checkout.
Closure: reject/propagate failed catch-up before acquiring or rewriting custody, and ensure its consumer cannot report a correction result as successful catch-up; keep inventory statements aligned. Permanent evidence should generalize the existing failed-attach invariant across both custody-acquiring attach paths, asserting failure leaves custody unchanged. A focused real-store test suffices; no cross-database transaction is demanded.
Repair material: YES (custody and failure-result semantics).

S3 BLOCKING — Checkpoint no-clobber repair falls back to a clobbering rename.
Invariant/authority: materializeSnapshot's operative destination-safe/atomic contract at packages/core/src/persistence/checkpoint/store.ts:59-63 refuses overwriting an existing destination; owning item #13 explicitly repairs the check-to-publication race, and ADR 0020 section 3 preserves persistence integrity.
Location: packages/core/src/persistence/checkpoint/store.ts:152-154; conflicting inventory guarantee at packages/core/src/rules/deterministicCapabilityInventory.ts:2032.
Concrete scenario: on a destination filesystem or policy that rejects hard links with EPERM, ENOTSUP, or EOPNOTSUPP, another actor creates the destination after the initial existsSync check. linkSync throws the unsupported/permission error, and renameSync overwrites that destination on platforms with replacement rename semantics. The extracted actual publication function reproduced replacement for all three fallback codes. There is not even another existence check in this fallback; adding one alone would retain the same race.
Boundary/owner: checkpoint publication, reached by restoreToNewWorkingCopy and forkFromCheckpoint and both CLI checkpoint commands; arbitrary user-selected destination paths are accepted.
Sibling analysis: the normal hard-link/EEXIST path safely refuses and other errors fail closed; both restore and fork share this one publication helper. The new race regression tests only the supported-hard-link EEXIST path. The inventory says a destination created in between is not replaced without disclosing the unsafe fallback, and its operation still describes rename as the normal publication.
Closure: preserve atomic no-clobber on every allowed publication path (fail closed if the filesystem cannot support it, or use an actually equivalent primitive), and correct related inventory/implementation descriptions. Permanent evidence should be a generalized publication invariant varying EEXIST and unsupported/permission fallback outcomes while asserting destination preservation and temporary-file cleanup. A small fault-injection test extends the existing race evidence proportionately.
Repair material: YES (persistence failure behavior/platform contract).

S4 BLOCKING — Proficiency inventory still overstates the Expertise refusal.
Invariant/authority: this review's explicit scope requires inventory statement updates to match repaired code; owning DESIGN's inventory update and ADR 0020 section 3 require truthful bounded capability/exclusion claims.
Location: packages/core/src/rules/deterministicCapabilityInventory.ts:1761; actual changed mechanism packages/core/src/character/proficiencyGrants.ts:200-225.
Concrete scenario: apply A then B, both granting Deception, select Expertise in Deception, and remove A with B still held. A recorded Deception, but the repair transfers it to B before the Expertise check, so removal succeeds. The inventory still says removal refuses when a recorded skill has Expertise. Actual-source probe verified success with the surviving heir and refusal without one.
Boundary/owner: maintained internal capability inventory, read as the bounded implementation statement; the runtime behavior is correct because the proficiency survives.
Sibling analysis: skills/saving throws/armor transfer correctly, chained A->B->C provenance works, and level-up persists the resulting ledger. Expertise refusal applies to the subset actually being dropped, not the original recorded set. Other changed inventory claims were compared to their implementations; checkout and checkpoint discrepancies are covered in S1/S3.
Closure: state that refusal occurs only when removal would actually lose an Expertise prerequisite after shared-source retention. Permanent evidence: existing generalized grant/removal tests plus bounded review of the corrected inventory wording are proportionate; no dedicated prose-matching test or new proof framework is required.
Repair material: NO if confined to this inventory clarification.

S5 BLOCKING — Combat-close model description still misstates the F3 boundary.
Invariant/authority: owning items #1/#10 select model-facing contract truthfulness; ADR 0020 section 3 requires bounded operation/exclusion claims to describe actual behavior, and ToolRegistry.definitions exposes this description directly to provider-neutral model adapters.
Location: packages/core/src/orchestrator/toolCloseCombatInstance.ts:23-27; actual behavior packages/core/src/state/activeEffects.ts:6918-6989,6758-6805,7139-7155.
Concrete scenarios: (a) put a remaining live until-removed condition/effect target on a combatant backed by a durable campaign actor, then close combat. The live target and condition link rebind onto that actor and persist; the description still unconditionally says effect targets/condition projections are removed, with its exception limited to owned summon links. (b) a character-owned round timer anchored to the closing instance expires on close, despite the unqualified claim 'Character-owned effects survive'. Existing permanent activeEffects.test.ts:4351-4434 directly demonstrates a round effect on a PC expiring and its condition being cleaned.
Boundary/owner: model-facing close_combat_instance description; every native tool-definition consumer sees it and may narrate or plan against these incorrect promises. The inventory already correctly describes timer settlement and rebinding of every live reference.
Sibling analysis: examined full closure precedence (round/participant timers first; combatant-owned concentration; durable references; remaining instance-only cleanup), ordinary campaign-actor combatants as well as bonded summons, targets/condition/actor/source references, and character effects with and without anchored timers. Effect-layer refusal mapping is repaired correctly and still rethrows programming errors.
Closure: describe timer settlement and limit target/condition removal to instance-only references; explain durable-reference retention and qualify which character effects survive. Preserve existing runtime behavior. Permanent evidence is the existing generalized closure/expiry and durable-lifecycle coverage, with proportionate description checks if needed; no new closure engine or exhaustive text snapshots are required.
Repair material: NO if description/evidence only; YES if runtime semantics are changed instead.
